Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
255 PM EDT Sun Sep 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 255 PM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 255 PM EDT Sunday...

1. The nor'easter exits the region tomorrow night, and 
conditions trend warmer and sunnier.  

2. Next chance of showers will be from a cold frontal passage 
Thursday night into Friday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 255 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The nor'easter made "landfall" this morning on the 
Jersey Shore, continuing to gradually weaken. Due to this and its 
completed occlusion, the weakening process will continue. The low 
will begin to re-enter the synoptic circulation tomorrow and drift 
northeastward into the Gulf of Maine and the Canadian Maritimes. 
Even though the precipitation shield will become smaller and more 
isolated as it weakens, the showers will continue over the region as 
the center passes closer. The showers will exit tomorrow night as 
the low continues to push northeast. Even though the rain will end 
for Tuesday, the boundary layer flow will transition to 
northwesterly and become increasingly blocked as the inversion 
height lowers, and cloud cover looks to hold thick in many areas, 
especially across the upslope areas and northern Vermont. Drier air 
will eventually mix into the lower levels for Wednesday and the sun 
should finally return for everywhere, though high clouds will begin 
to increase in the afternoon from a storm system moving toward the 
region from the Midwest. Due to the sunshine, temperatures should 
rise into the 70s for most areas on Wednesday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: High pressure builds into our region from the south on 
Thursday providing us with the warmest day of the forecast period. 
Maximum temperatures will range through the 70s with some sites 
having near record warmth. Thursday night into Friday will bring our 
next chance for precipitation as a cold front will cross our region 
in that timeframe. Another ridge of surface high pressure will build 
into our area behind this front bringing additional dry weather, 
this time with cooler temperatures as the high builds into our area 
from Canada.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 18Z Monday...Scattered rain showers continue at our TAF
sites today, with the greatest impacts at our southern and 
eastern TAF sites including BTV/RUT/MPV/EFK. Ceilings and vsby 
will mostly remain MVFR or better. Best chances for occasional 
MVFR conditions and HIR TRRN OBSCD during the daylight hours 
today will be at RUT and MPV, and mainly due to ceilings. Winds 
will generally be N to NE, with gusts 20-25kt becoming 
increasingly common during the daylight hours. During periods in
which stronger wind gusts don't reach the surface, it appears 
that pockets of LLWS will be possible. MSS should be northwest 
of most of the shower and LLWS activity and is expected to 
remain VFR through the TAF period. 

Outlook...

Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
